a new approach to calculate the energy of the ground state in a pairing model with an arbitrary number of levels.
a study of the ground state of the pairing Hamiltonian in the strong-couple regime, which is relevant to the description of the nuclear superfluid phase transition.

the ground-state energy of an exactly solvable two-level pairing model, and the energies of the first 0+ and 1- states are also calculated using several approximations, such as the BCS, LN method, RPA, QRPA, RRPA, and RQRPA.

the RRPA and/or RQRPA with the LN pairing gap is a good approximation for the strong coupling regime.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, for the strong-coupled pairing model, the RPA and QRPA are the best approximations, and the RRPA and the RQRPA are the best among all the RPA-type approximations.

the LN method and QRPA give a reasonable description of the ground-state properties of superconducting systems in the strong-couple regime, while the LN method and RRPA give a reasonable account of the ground-state and the first excited 1- state in the weak-coupling regime.

the QRPA with the pairing gap calculated by the LN method is a good approximation for the ground state of a pairing system in the strong-couple regime, and the RRPA and the RQRPA are the best choices for the first excited 1 + state.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in order to obtain a good description of the ground-state and the excited-state energies, it is necessary to include the renormalization effect in the RPA.
, in order to describe a superconducting system, one should use the RRPA or RQRPA in conjunction with the LN method.

, in the strongly correlated pairing system, the RQRPA and RRPA in combination with a suitable pairing gap given by LN method can offer a good description of the ground-state and the first excited 1 + state in the strong-couple regime.
